Based on the provided context, a general-purpose AI model is classified as having systemic risk if it meets any of the following conditions:
(a) It has high impact capabilities evaluated on the basis of appropriate technical tools and methodologies, including indicators and benchmarks; 
(b) Based on a decision of the Commission, ex officio or following a qualified alert from the scientific panel, it has capabilities or an impact equivalent to those set out in point (a) having regard to the criteria set out in Annex XIII.

Regarding whether the provider can challenge it:
- A provider of a general-purpose AI model that meets the condition referred to in Article 51(1), point (a), may present, with its notification, sufficiently substantiated arguments to demonstrate that, exceptionally, although it meets that requirement, the model does not present, due to its specific characteristics, systemic risks and therefore should not be classified as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk. 
- Additionally, upon a reasoned request containing objective, detailed, and new reasons that have arisen since the designation decision (which can be requested at the earliest six months after the designation decision), a provider whose model has been designated as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk may request that the Commission reassess whether the model can still be considered to present systemic risks on the basis of the criteria set out in Annex XIII.
